stem:
Madhav draws transversal $w$ across lines $u$ and $v$. A pair of corresponding angles each measures $55^\circ$.

Which two claims are correct?

One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Equal corresponding angles mean $u \parallel v$ on the page.
Call the answer the words parallel lines only, without using the equal $55^\circ$ corresponding angles as the test.
If $u \parallel v$, then corresponding angles are equal, so the matching angle at the other line is also $55^\circ$.
The equal $55^\circ$ marks decide that transversal $w$ must be drawn before any parallel test can be stated.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal corresponding angles imply $u \parallel v$, and if the lines are parallel then corresponding angles stay equal at $55^\circ$. Naming only "parallel lines", or treating the equal marks as choosing the transversal first, leaves that hinge.
